title.zh: 卷二百六十八 列傳第一百五十六 曹文詔 周遇吉 黃得功
title.en: Volume 268 Biographies 156: Cao Wenzhao, Zhou Yuji, Huang Degong
title.raw: 卷二百六十八 列傳第一百五十六 曹文詔 周遇吉 黃得功 Volume 268 Biographies 156: Cao Wenzhao, Zhou Yuji, Huang Degong

sentences.zh: 曹文詔

translations.literal: Cao Wenzhao
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wenzhao

sentences.zh: （弟文耀）〉

translations.literal: (younger brother Wenyao)〉
translations.idiomatic: (his younger brother Wenyao)]

sentences.zh: 周遇吉黃得功

translations.literal: Zhou Yuji Huang Degong
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yuji and Huang Degong

sentences.zh: 曹文詔，大同人。

translations.literal: Cao Wenzhao was a man of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wenzhao was a native of Datong.

sentences.zh: 勇毅有智略。

translations.literal: Brave, resolute, and possessed of strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He was brave, resolute, and strategically gifted.

sentences.zh: 從軍遼左，歷事熊廷弼、孫承宗，積功至遊擊。

translations.literal: He joined the army in eastern Liaodong, served under Xiong Tingbi and Sun Chengzong, and through accumulated merit rose to roaming striker.
translations.idiomatic: He entered military service in eastern Liaodong, served under Xiong Tingbi and Sun Chengzong, and through accumulated merit was promoted to roaming striker.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年冬，從袁崇煥入衛京師。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Chongzhen, he followed Yuan Chonghuan to defend the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of the Chongzhen reign, he followed Yuan Chonghuan to the defense of the capital.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，總理馬世龍畀所賜尚方劍，令率參將王承胤、張叔嘉、都司左良玉等伏玉田、枯樹、洪橋，鏖戰有功，遷參將。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year, the supreme commander Ma Shilong gave him the imperial sword he had been granted and ordered him to lead deputy generals Wang Chengyin, Zhang Shujia, bureau commander Zuo Liangyu, and others to lie in ambush at Yutian, Kushu, and Hongqiao; he fought fiercely with merit and was transferred to deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: The following February, supreme commander Ma Shilong entrusted him with the imperial sword he had received and ordered him to lead deputy generals Wang Chengyin, Zhang Shujia, bureau commander Zuo Liangyu, and others in ambush at Yutian, Kushu, and Hongqiao. After fierce fighting with notable success, he was promoted to deputy general.

sentences.zh: 自大塹山轉戰逼遵化，又從世龍等克大安城及鮎魚諸關。

translations.literal: From Dachan Mountain he turned to fight and pressed toward Zunhua, and again followed Shilong and others to capture Da'an City and the various passes of Nianyu.
translations.idiomatic: He fought his way from Dachan Mountain toward Zunhua, then joined Shilong and others in capturing Da'an City and the Nianyu passes.

sentences.zh: 以與復四城功，加都督僉事。

translations.literal: For his merit in recovering the four cities, he was given the additional title of vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: For his part in recovering the four cities, he was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 七月，陜西賊熾，擢延綏東路副總兵。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, when Shaanxi bandits flared up, he was promoted to deputy regional commander of the eastern Yan'an route.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, as rebellion in Shaanxi intensified, he was appointed deputy regional commander of the eastern Yan'an route.

sentences.zh: 賊渠王嘉胤久據河曲。

translations.literal: The bandit chieftain Wang Jiayin had long held Hequ.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leader Wang Jiayin had long held Hequ.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，文詔克其城。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year, Wenzhao captured his city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourth year, Wenzhao took the city.

sentences.zh: 嘉胤脫走，轉掠至陽城南山。

translations.literal: Jiayin escaped and turned to plunder as far as the southern mountains of Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayin broke free and ranged south as far as the Yangcheng hills.

sentences.zh: 文詔追及之，其下斬以降，以功擢臨洮總兵官。

translations.literal: Wenzhao overtook him; his followers beheaded him to surrender, and for this merit he was promoted to regional commander of Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao caught up with him; his followers killed him and submitted. For this achievement Wenzhao was appointed regional commander of Lintao.

sentences.zh: 點燈子自陜入山西。

translations.literal: Lamp-Lighter entered Shanxi from Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Lamp-Lighter crossed from Shaanxi into Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 文詔追之，及於稷山，諭降七百人。

translations.literal: Wenzhao pursued him, caught him at Jishan, and persuaded seven hundred men to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao pursued him to Jishan and induced seven hundred men to surrender.

sentences.zh: 點燈子遁，尋被獲，伏誅。

translations.literal: Lamp-Lighter fled, was soon captured, and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Lamp-Lighter escaped but was soon captured and put to death.

sentences.zh: 李老柴、獨行狼陷中部，巡撫練國事、延綏總兵王承恩圍之。

translations.literal: Li Laochai and Lone Wolf seized Zhongbu; Grand Coordinator Lian Guoshi and Yan'an regional commander Wang Chengen besieged them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Laochai and Lone Wolf overran Zhongbu; Grand Coordinator Lian Guoshi and Yan'an regional commander Wang Chengen laid siege to them.

sentences.zh: 五月，慶陽賊郝臨庵、劉道江援之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Qingyang bandits Hao Lin'an and Liu Daojiang came to their relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, the Qingyang rebels Hao Lin'an and Liu Daojiang marched to relieve them.

sentences.zh: 會文詔西旋，與榆林參政張福臻合剿，馘老柴及其黨一條龍，余黨奔摩雲谷。

translations.literal: Just then Wenzhao was returning west; he joined Yulin administrator Zhang Fuzhen in a joint suppression, beheaded Laochai and his follower One Dragon, and the remaining bandits fled to Moyun Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao was then returning westward; he joined Yulin administrator Zhang Fuzhen in a joint campaign, killed Laochai and his follower One Dragon, and drove the rest toward Moyun Valley.

sentences.zh: 副將張弘業、遊擊李明輔戰死。

translations.literal: Deputy general Zhang Hongye and roaming striker Li Mingfu died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy general Zhang Hongye and roaming striker Li Mingfu were killed in action.

sentences.zh: 文詔乃與遊擊左光先、崔宗蔭、李國奇分剿綏德、宜君、清澗、米脂賊，戰懷寧川、黑泉峪、封家溝、綿湖峪，皆大捷，掃地王授首。

translations.literal: Wenzhao then with roaming strikers Zuo Guangxian, Cui Zongyin, and Li Guoqi divided forces to suppress bandits in Suide, Yijun, Qingjian, and Mizhi; they fought at Huaining River, Heiquan Pass, Fengjiagou, and Mianhu Valley, all great victories, and Sweeps-the-Earth King was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao then divided forces with roaming strikers Zuo Guangxian, Cui Zongyin, and Li Guoqi to hunt rebels in Suide, Yijun, Qingjian, and Mizhi. Battles at Huaining River, Heiquan Pass, Fengjiagou, and Mianhu Valley all ended in decisive victories, and Sweeps-the-Earth King was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 紅軍友、李都司、杜三、楊老柴者，神一魁余黨也，屯鎮原，將犯平涼。

translations.literal: Red Army Friend, Li Dusi, Du Three, and Yang Laochai were remnant followers of Shen Yikui; they encamped at Zhenyuan and were about to attack Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Red Army Friend, Li Dusi, Du Three, and Yang Laochai were survivors of Shen Yikui's faction. They held Zhenyuan and were preparing to strike Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 國事檄甘肅總兵楊嘉謨、副將王性善扼之，賊走慶陽。

translations.literal: Guoshi dispatched orders to Gansu regional commander Yang Jiamo and deputy general Wang Xingshan to block them, and the bandits fled to Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guoshi ordered Gansu regional commander Yang Jiamo and deputy general Wang Xingshan to intercept them, and the rebels retreated toward Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 文詔從鄜州間道與嘉謨、性善合。

translations.literal: Wenzhao took a bypath from Fuzhou and joined Jiamo and Xingshan.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao took a hidden route from Fuzhou and united with Jiamo and Xingshan.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，大戰西濠，斬千級，生擒杜三、楊老柴。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year they fought a great battle at Ximao, beheaded a thousand, and captured Du Three and Yang Laochai alive.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year they fought a major battle at Ximao, killing a thousand rebels and taking Du Three and Yang Laochai alive.

sentences.zh: 余黨糾他賊掠武安監，陷華亭，攻莊浪。

translations.literal: The remaining followers gathered other bandits to plunder Wu'an Post, seized Huating, and attacked Zhuanglang.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors rallied other rebels, raided Wu'an Post, overran Huating, and attacked Zhuanglang.

sentences.zh: 文詔、嘉謨至，賊屯張麻村。

translations.literal: When Wenzhao and Jiamo arrived, the bandits encamped at Zhangma Village.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzhao and Jiamo arrived, the rebels were encamped at Zhangma Village.

sentences.zh: 官軍掩擊，賊走高山。

translations.literal: The government army struck by surprise, and the bandits fled to the high mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Government forces struck by surprise, and the rebels fled into the high mountains.

sentences.zh: 遊擊曹變蛟、馮舉、劉成功、平安等噪而上，賊潰走。

translations.literal: Roaming strikers Cao Bianjiao, Feng Ju, Liu Chenggong, Ping An, and others charged up with a shout, and the bandits broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Roaming strikers Cao Bianjiao, Feng Ju, Liu Chenggong, Ping An, and others charged uphill with a roar, and the rebels broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 變蛟者，文詔從子也。

translations.literal: Bianjiao was Wenzhao's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Bianjiao was Wenzhao's nephew.

sentences.zh: 會性善及甘肅副將李鴻嗣、參將莫與京等至，共擊斬五百二十余級。

translations.literal: When Xingshan and Gansu deputy general Li Hongsi, deputy general Mo Yujing, and others arrived, they joined the attack and beheaded more than five hundred twenty.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingshan arrived with Gansu deputy general Li Hongsi, deputy general Mo Yujing, and others, the combined force killed more than five hundred twenty rebels.

sentences.zh: 追敗之鹹寧關，又敗之關上嶺。

translations.literal: They pursued and defeated them at Xianning Pass and again at Guanshang Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued and routed them at Xianning Pass and again at Guanshang Ridge.

sentences.zh: 追至隴安，嘉謨、變蛟夾擊，復敗之。

translations.literal: Pursuing to Long'an, Jiamo and Bianjiao attacked from both sides and defeated them again.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit reached Long'an, where Jiamo and Bianjiao attacked from both flanks and defeated them again.

sentences.zh: 賊余眾數千欲走漢南，為遊擊趙光遠所遏，乃由長寧驛走張家川。

translations.literal: Several thousand remaining bandits wished to flee to southern Han, but were blocked by roaming striker Zhao Guangyuan, so they went by way of Changning Post toward Zhangjiachuan.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand survivors tried to flee south into Han territory but were blocked by roaming striker Zhao Guangyuan and turned instead toward Zhangjiachuan by way of Changning Post.

sentences.zh: 其逸出清水者，副將蔣一陽遇之敗，都司李宮用被執。

translations.literal: Those who slipped out at Qingshui were met and defeated by deputy general Jiang Yiyang, and bureau commander Li Gongyong was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Those who broke out at Qingshui were defeated by deputy general Jiang Yiyang, and bureau commander Li Gongyong was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 文詔乃縱反間，紿其黨，殺紅軍友，遂蹙敗之水落城。

translations.literal: Wenzhao then spread counter-intelligence, deceived their followers, had Red Army Friend killed, and thus pressed them to defeat at Shuiluo City.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao then used counter-intelligence to deceive the rebel ranks, had Red Army Friend killed, and drove the rest to defeat at Shuiluo City.

sentences.zh: 追至靜寧州，賊奔據唐毛山，變蛟先登，殄其眾。

translations.literal: Pursuing to Jingning Prefecture, the bandits fled to hold Tangmao Mountain; Bianjiao was first to ascend and annihilated their force.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit reached Jingning Prefecture, where the rebels fled to Tangmao Mountain. Bianjiao was first up the slope and wiped out their force.

sentences.zh: 可天飛、郝臨庵，劉道江為王承恩所敗，退保鐵角城。

translations.literal: Ke Tianfei, Hao Lin'an, and Liu Daojiang were defeated by Wang Chengen and withdrew to defend Tie'ao City.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Tianfei, Hao Lin'an, and Liu Daojiang were beaten by Wang Chengen and fell back to defend Tie'ao City.

sentences.zh: 獨行狼、李都司走與合，可天飛、劉道江遂圍合水。

translations.literal: Lone Wolf and Li Dusi fled to join them, and Ke Tianfei and Liu Daojiang then besieged Heshui.
translations.idiomatic: Lone Wolf and Li Dusi fled to join them, after which Ke Tianfei and Liu Daojiang laid siege to Heshui.

sentences.zh: 文詔往救。

translations.literal: Wenzhao went to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao marched to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 賊匿精銳，以千騎逆戰，誘抵南原，伏大起。

translations.literal: The bandits hid their elite troops, met him with a thousand horsemen, lured him to the southern plain, and then their ambush rose in force.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels concealed their best troops, met him with a thousand horsemen, lured him onto the southern plain, and then sprang a massive ambush.

sentences.zh: 城上人言曹將軍已歿。

translations.literal: Those on the walls said General Cao was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: Men on the city walls cried that General Cao was already dead.

sentences.zh: 文詔持矛左右突，匹馬縈萬眾中。

translations.literal: Wenzhao held his spear and charged left and right, a lone horse wheeling through tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao charged left and right with his spear, a lone rider wheeling through a sea of enemies.

sentences.zh: 諸軍望見，夾擊，賊大敗，僵屍蔽野，余走銅川橋。

translations.literal: The armies saw him and attacked from both sides; the bandits were greatly defeated, corpses covered the field, and the remainder fled to Tongchuan Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The troops saw him and attacked from both flanks. The rebels were routed, the field strewn with corpses, and the survivors fled toward Tongchuan Bridge.

sentences.zh: 文詔率變蛟、舉、嘉謨及參將方茂功等追及之，大戰陷陣，賊復大敗。

translations.literal: Wenzhao led Bianjiao, Ju, Jiamo, and deputy general Fang Maogong and others in pursuit, fought a great battle breaking into their ranks, and the bandits were again greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao led Bianjiao, Ju, Jiamo, deputy general Fang Maogong, and others in pursuit, smashed into their ranks, and routed them again.

sentences.zh: 尋與寧夏總兵賀虎臣、固原總兵楊麒破賊甘泉之虎兕凹。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, together with Ningxia regional commander He Huchen and Guyuan regional commander Yang Qi, he defeated the bandits at Husi'ao in Ganquan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he joined Ningxia regional commander He Huchen and Guyuan regional commander Yang Qi in defeating the rebels at Husi'ao in Ganquan.

sentences.zh: 麒復追賊安口河、崇信窯、白茅山，皆大獲。

translations.literal: Qi again pursued the bandits at Ankou River, Chongxin Kiln, and Baimao Mountain, all with great gains.
translations.idiomatic: Qi pursued them again at Ankou River, Chongxin Kiln, and Baimao Mountain, winning major victories each time.

sentences.zh: 總督洪承疇斬可天飛、李都司於平涼，降其將白廣恩，余賊分竄。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Hong Chengchou beheaded Ke Tianfei and Li Dusi at Pingliang, accepted the surrender of their general Bai Guang'en, and the remaining bandits scattered in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Hong Chengchou executed Ke Tianfei and Li Dusi at Pingliang, accepted the surrender of their general Bai Guang'en, and the remaining rebels scattered.

sentences.zh: 文詔追擊之隴州、平、鳳間。

translations.literal: Wenzhao pursued them between Longzhou, Pingliang, and Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao pursued them through the country between Longzhou, Pingliang, and Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 十月三戰三敗之，遂蹙賊耀州錐子山，其黨殺獨行狼、郝臨庵以降。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he fought three battles and defeated them three times, then pressed the bandits to Zuizi Mountain in Yaozhou; their followers killed Lone Wolf and Hao Lin'an to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he fought three battles and won three victories, then cornered the rebels on Zuizi Mountain in Yaozhou, where their followers killed Lone Wolf and Hao Lin'an and submitted.

sentences.zh: 承疇戮四百人，余散遣。

translations.literal: Chengchou executed four hundred men and dispersed the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou executed four hundred men and released the rest.

sentences.zh: 關中巨寇略平。

translations.literal: The great bandits of Guanzhong were largely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The great rebel bands of Guanzhong were largely subdued.

sentences.zh: 巡撫御史範復粹匯奏首功凡三萬六千六百有奇，文詔功第一，嘉謨次之，承恩、麒又次之。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Censor Fan Fucui submitted a combined report of heads taken totaling more than thirty-six thousand six hundred; Wenzhao's merit ranked first, Jiamo second, and Chengen and Qi after them.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Censor Fan Fucui reported a combined tally of more than thirty-six thousand six hundred enemy heads. Wenzhao ranked first in merit, Jiamo second, and Chengen and Qi after them.

sentences.zh: 文詔在陜西，大小數十戰，功最多，承疇不為敘。

translations.literal: Wenzhao in Shaanxi fought several dozen battles large and small and achieved the most merit, but Chengchou did not record it.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaanxi Wenzhao fought several dozen engagements and won the greatest share of merit, yet Chengchou did not report his achievements.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史吳甡推獎甚至，復粹疏復上。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Wu Shen praised him to the utmost, and Fucui memorialized again on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Wu Shen praised him at length, and Fucui submitted another memorial on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 兵部抑其功，卒不敘。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War suppressed his merit, and in the end it was not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War downplayed his achievements, and in the end he received no formal recognition.

sentences.zh: 當是時，賊見陜兵盛，多流入山西，其魁紫金梁、混世王、姬關鎖、八大王、曹操、闖塌天、興加哈利七大部，多者萬人，少亦半之，蹂躪汾州、太原、平陽。

translations.literal: At this time, seeing Shaanxi troops strong, many bandits flowed into Shanxi; their chiefs were seven great hosts—Purple-Gold Beam, World-Ruiner King, Ji Gate-Lock, Eight Great King, Cao Cao, Rush-Collapse Heaven, and Xing Jia Hali—with ten thousand men at most and half that at least, trampling Fenzhou, Taiyuan, and Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the rebels, finding Shaanxi heavily garrisoned, poured into Shanxi in seven major bands led by Purple-Gold Beam, World-Ruiner King, Ji Gate-Lock, Eight Great King, Cao Cao, Rush-Collapse Heaven, and Xing Jia Hali. The largest numbered ten thousand men and the smallest half that, and they ravaged Fenzhou, Taiyuan, and Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 御史張宸極言：「賊自秦中來。

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Chen said: "The bandits come from within Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Chen said, "These rebels come from Qin territory.

sentences.zh: 秦將曹文詔威名宿著，士民為之謠曰『軍中有一曹，西賊聞之心膽搖』。

translations.literal: The Qin general Cao Wenzhao's renown is long established; soldiers and civilians have a song for him: 'In the army there is a Cao; when western bandits hear it, their hearts and gall tremble.'
translations.idiomatic: The Qin general Cao Wenzhao has long been famous, and soldiers and civilians sing of him: 'In the army there is a Cao; when western rebels hear his name, their hearts turn to water.'

sentences.zh: 且嘗立功晉中，而秦賊滅且盡。

translations.literal: Moreover he once achieved merit in Jin, and the Qin bandits were destroyed almost to the last.
translations.idiomatic: He has already won distinction in Jin, and the rebels of Qin have been nearly wiped out.

sentences.zh: 宜敕令入晉協剿。

translations.literal: He should be ordered by imperial command to enter Jin and join in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: He should be ordered into Jin to join the suppression campaign.

sentences.zh: 」於是命陜西、山西諸將並受文詔節制。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the command was issued that all generals of Shaanxi and Shanxi should come under Wenzhao's command.
translations.idiomatic: " The court then ordered all generals of Shaanxi and Shanxi to serve under Wenzhao's command.

sentences.zh: 六年正月抵霍州，敗賊汾河、盂系，追及於壽陽。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year he reached Huozhou, defeated the bandits on the Fen River and in the Yu region, and overtook them at Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year he reached Huozhou, defeated the rebels along the Fen River and in the Yu region, and overtook them at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 巡撫許鼎臣遣謀士張宰先大軍嘗賊，賊驚潰。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Xu Dingchen sent strategist Zhang Zai ahead of the main army to probe the bandits, and the bandits fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Xu Dingchen sent strategist Zhang Zai ahead of the main army to test the rebels, who broke and fled in alarm.

sentences.zh: 二月，文詔追擊之，斬混世王於碧霞村。

translations.literal: In the second month Wenzhao pursued them and beheaded World-Ruiner King at Bixia Village.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Wenzhao pursued them and killed World-Ruiner King at Bixia Village.

sentences.zh: 余黨為猛如虎逐走，遇文詔兵方山，復敗。

translations.literal: The remaining followers were driven off by Meng Ruhu, met Wenzhao's troops at Fangshan, and were defeated again.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors were driven off by Meng Ruhu, met Wenzhao's troops at Fangshan, and were defeated again.

sentences.zh: 五臺、盂、定襄、壽陽賊盡平。

translations.literal: The bandits of Wutai, Yu, Dingxiang, and Shouyang were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels of Wutai, Yu, Dingxiang, and Shouyang were all subdued.

sentences.zh: 鼎臣命文詔軍平定，備太原東，張應昌軍汾州，備太原西。

translations.literal: Dingchen ordered Wenzhao's army to hold Pingding and guard the east of Taiyuan, and Zhang Yingchang's army at Fenzhou to guard the west of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dingchen stationed Wenzhao's army at Pingding to guard eastern Taiyuan and Zhang Yingchang's army at Fenzhou to guard the west.

sentences.zh: 文詔連敗賊太谷、範村、榆社，太原賊幾盡。

translations.literal: Wenzhao repeatedly defeated the bandits at Taigu, Fancun, and Yushe, and the Taiyuan bandits were nearly gone.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao defeated the rebels in succession at Taigu, Fancun, and Yushe, and the rebels around Taiyuan were nearly eliminated.

sentences.zh: 帝以文詔功多，敕所過地多積糗糧以犒，並敕文詔速平賊。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Wenzhao's merits were many, ordered the places he passed to store much dried grain to reward him, and also ordered Wenzhao to pacify the bandits quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wenzhao's achievements were so great, the emperor ordered the districts he passed through to stock dried provisions for his troops and commanded him to pacify the rebels quickly.

sentences.zh: 山西監視中官劉中允言文詔剿賊徐溝、盂、定襄，所司不給米，反以炮石傷士卒。

translations.literal: Shanxi supervising eunuch Liu Zhongyun said that when Wenzhao suppressed bandits at Xugou, Yu, and Dingxiang, the responsible offices gave no rice and instead wounded the soldiers with cannon stones.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi supervising eunuch Liu Zhongyun reported that while Wenzhao was suppressing rebels at Xugou, Yu, and Dingxiang, local officials failed to supply grain and even injured his soldiers with artillery.

sentences.zh: 帝即下御史按問。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately sent censors to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately dispatched censors to investigate.

sentences.zh: 三月，賊從河內上太行，文詔大敗之澤州。

translations.literal: In the third month the bandits ascended the Taihang from Henei, and Wenzhao greatly defeated them at Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the rebels climbed the Taihang from Henei, and Wenzhao routed them at Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 賊走潞安，文詔至陽城遇賊不擊，自沁水潛師，還擊之芹地、劉村寨，斬首千余。

translations.literal: The bandits fled to Lu'an; Wenzhao reached Yangcheng, met the bandits but did not attack, secretly moved his army from Qinshui, and struck them again at Qindi and Liucunzhai, beheading more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled to Lu'an. Wenzhao reached Yangcheng, met them but held back, then moved troops secretly from Qinshui and struck them at Qindi and Liucunzhai, killing more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 四月，賊屯潤城，其他部陷平順，殺知縣徐明揚。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the bandits encamped at Runcheng; another band seized Pingshun and killed magistrate Xu Mingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the rebels encamped at Runcheng while another band overran Pingshun and killed magistrate Xu Mingyang.

sentences.zh: 文詔至，賊走，乃夜半襲潤城，斬賊千五百。

translations.literal: When Wenzhao arrived the bandits fled; he then raided Runcheng at midnight and beheaded fifteen hundred bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzhao arrived the rebels fled, so he raided Runcheng at midnight and killed fifteen hundred of them.

sentences.zh: 紫金梁、老回回自榆社走武鄉，過天星走高澤山，文詔皆擊敗。

translations.literal: Purple-Gold Beam and Old Huihui fled from Yushe to Wuxiang, Crossing Heaven Star went to Gaozeshan, and Wenzhao defeated them all.
translations.idiomatic: Purple-Gold Beam and Old Huihui fled from Yushe toward Wuxiang, Crossing Heaven Star toward Gaozeshan, and Wenzhao defeated them all.

sentences.zh: 他賊圍涉縣，聞文詔破賊黎城，解去。

translations.literal: Other bandits besieged She County; hearing that Wenzhao had defeated bandits at Licheng, they lifted the siege and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Other rebels were besieging She County, but when they heard that Wenzhao had defeated a rebel force at Licheng, they raised the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 五月，帝遣中官孫茂霖為文詔內中軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the emperor sent eunuch Sun Maolin to serve as Wenzhao's internal army commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the emperor appointed eunuch Sun Maolin as Wenzhao's internal army commander.

sentences.zh: 賊犯沁水，文詔大敗之，擒其魁大虎，又敗之遼城毛嶺山西。

translations.literal: The bandits attacked Qinshui; Wenzhao greatly defeated them, captured their chief Great Tiger, and again defeated them west of Liaocheng Maoling.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels attacked Qinshui, Wenzhao routed them, captured their leader Great Tiger, and defeated them again west of Liaocheng Maoling.

sentences.zh: 賊既屢敗，乃避文詔鋒，多流入河北。

translations.literal: Having been repeatedly defeated, the bandits avoided Wenzhao's edge and many flowed into Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated defeats the rebels avoided Wenzhao's spearhead and poured into Hebei.

sentences.zh: 帝乃命文詔移師往討。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Wenzhao to move his army to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Wenzhao to march into Hebei against them.

sentences.zh: 而賊已敗鄧玘兵於林縣，文詔率五營軍夜襲破之。

translations.literal: The bandits had already defeated Deng Yin's troops at Lin County; Wenzhao led the five-camp army in a night raid and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had already defeated Deng Yin's force at Lin County, but Wenzhao led his five-camp army in a night attack and shattered them.

sentences.zh: 七月大敗懷慶賊柴陵村，馘其魁滾地龍，又追斬老回回於濟源。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he greatly defeated the Huaiqing bandits at Chailing Village, beheaded their chief Rolling Earth Dragon, and again pursued and beheaded Old Huihui at Jiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he routed the Huaiqing rebels at Chailing Village, killed their leader Rolling Earth Dragon, and pursued Old Huihui to Jiyuan and killed him there.

sentences.zh: 文詔在洪洞時，與裏居御史劉令譽忤。

translations.literal: When Wenzhao was at Hongtong he had a falling-out with retired censor Liu Lingyu.
translations.idiomatic: While stationed at Hongtong, Wenzhao had fallen out with retired censor Liu Lingyu.

sentences.zh: 及是，令譽按河南，而四川石矽土官馬鳳儀軍敗沒於侯家莊，賴文詔馳退賊。

translations.literal: At this time Lingyu was investigating Henan, while the Sichuan native-official Ma Fengyi of Shixi was destroyed in battle at Houjiazhuang; it was thanks to Wenzhao's rapid march that the bandits were driven off.
translations.idiomatic: By then Lingyu was investigating Henan, while the Sichuan native-official Ma Fengyi of Shixi had been wiped out at Houjiazhuang. Only Wenzhao's rapid march drove the rebels back.

sentences.zh: 甫解甲，與令譽相見，語復相失。

translations.literal: Just after laying aside his armor he met Lingyu, and their words again clashed.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely doffed his armor when he met Lingyu, and their words clashed again.

sentences.zh: 文詔拂衣起，面叱之。

translations.literal: Wenzhao brushed his robe and rose, rebuking him to his face.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao rose abruptly and rebuked him to his face.

sentences.zh: 令譽怒，遂以鳳儀之敗為文詔罪。

translations.literal: Lingyu was angry and then made Fengyi's defeat Wenzhao's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Lingyu blamed Fengyi's defeat on Wenzhao.

sentences.zh: 部議文詔怙勝而騎，乃調之大同。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated that Wenzhao relied on victory and was arrogant on horseback, and transferred him to Datong.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry ruled that Wenzhao had grown arrogant in victory, and he was transferred to Datong.

sentences.zh: 七年七月，大清兵西征插漢，還師入大同境，攻拔得勝堡、參將李全自經，遂攻圍懷仁縣及井坪堡、應州。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the seventh year the Great Qing army campaigned west against Chakhar, returned and entered Datong territory, captured Desheng Fort, deputy general Li Quan hanged himself, and they then attacked and besieged Huairen County as well as Jingping Fort and Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the seventh year the Qing army marched west against Chakhar, then returned into Datong territory, took Desheng Fort, and deputy general Li Quan hanged himself. They went on to besiege Huairen County, Jingping Fort, and Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 文詔偕總督張宗衡先駐懷仁固守。

translations.literal: Wenzhao together with Grand Coordinator Zhang Zongheng first stationed at Huairen to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao and Grand Coordinator Zhang Zongheng took post at Huairen to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 八月，圍解，即移駐鎮城，挑戰敗還。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the siege was lifted; he then moved to garrison Zhencheng, challenged the enemy, was defeated, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the siege was lifted. He then moved to Zhencheng, offered battle, was beaten back, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 已而靈丘及他屯堡多失陷，大清兵亦旋。

translations.literal: Before long Lingqiu and many other garrison forts fell, and the Great Qing army also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Lingqiu and many other border forts fell, and the Qing army withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 十一月論罪，文詔、宗衡及巡撫胡沾恩並充軍邊衛。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month guilt was determined; Wenzhao, Zongheng, and Grand Coordinator Hu Zhan'en were all sentenced to military exile on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month they were found guilty. Wenzhao, Zongheng, and Grand Coordinator Hu Zhan'en were all sentenced to military exile on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 令甫下，山西巡撫吳甡薦文詔知兵善戰，請用之晉中。

translations.literal: The order had just been issued when Shanxi Grand Coordinator Wu Shen recommended Wenzhao as knowing warfare and skilled in battle, and requested that he be used in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The order had barely been issued when Shanxi Grand Coordinator Wu Shen recommended Wenzhao as a skilled commander and asked that he be employed in Jin.

sentences.zh: 乃命為援剿總兵官，立功自贖。

translations.literal: He was then appointed relief-suppression regional commander, to redeem himself through merit.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed relief-suppression regional commander, with orders to redeem himself through merit.

sentences.zh: 當是時，河南禍尤劇，帝已允兵部議，敕文詔馳剿河南賊。

translations.literal: At that time, disaster in Henan was especially severe. The emperor had already approved the Ministry of War's proposal and ordered Wenzhao by imperial edict to hurry south and suppress the Henan bandits.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the crisis in Henan was especially grave. The emperor had already approved the Ministry of War's plan and ordered Wenzhao to ride south at once to suppress the rebels in Henan.

sentences.zh: 甡復抗疏力爭，請令先平晉賊，後入豫，帝不許。

translations.literal: Shen again submitted a memorial contesting this forcefully, requesting that he first pacify the Jin bandits and afterward enter Yu; the emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shen submitted another memorial arguing forcefully that Wenzhao should first pacify the rebels in Shanxi before entering Henan. The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 而文詔以甡有恩，竟取道太原，為甡所留。

translations.literal: But Wenzhao, owing Shen a debt of gratitude, still took the route through Taiyuan and was detained by Shen.
translations.idiomatic: But Wenzhao, grateful to Wu Shen for his earlier support, nevertheless routed his march through Taiyuan, where Shen detained him.

sentences.zh: 會賊高加計已殲，而鳳陽告陷，遂整兵南，以八年三月會總督洪承疇於信陽。

translations.literal: It happened that the bandit Gao Jiaji had already been destroyed, but Fengyang reported its fall, so he reorganized his troops and marched south; in the third month of the eighth year he joined Governor-General Hong Chengchou at Xinyang.
translations.idiomatic: By then the rebel Gao Jiaji had already been wiped out, but word came that Fengyang had fallen. Wenzhao reorganized his forces and marched south, joining Governor-General Hong Chengchou at Xinyang in the third month of the eighth year.

sentences.zh: 承疇大喜，即令擊賊隨州，文詔追斬賊三百八十有奇。

translations.literal: Chengchou was greatly pleased and immediately ordered an attack on the bandits at Suizhou. Wenzhao pursued and beheaded more than three hundred and eighty bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou was delighted and immediately ordered an assault on the rebels at Suizhou. Wenzhao pursued them and killed more than three hundred and eighty.

sentences.zh: 四月，承疇次汝州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Chengchou encamped at Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Chengchou made camp at Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 以賊盡入關中，議還顧根本。

translations.literal: Because the bandits had all entered Guanzhong, they discussed returning to safeguard the core region.
translations.idiomatic: Since the rebels had all poured into Guanzhong, the commanders debated turning back to protect the heartland.

sentences.zh: 分命諸將扼要害，檄文詔入關，文詔乃馳至靈寶謁承疇。

translations.literal: He divided orders among the generals to hold key points and dispatched Wenzhao to enter the pass. Wenzhao then galloped to Lingbao to pay his respects to Chengchou.
translations.idiomatic: He assigned his generals to hold the critical passes and summoned Wenzhao into the pass. Wenzhao rode at once to Lingbao to report to Chengchou.

sentences.zh: 承疇以賊在商、雒，聞官兵至，必先走漢中，而大軍由潼關入，反在其後，乃令文詔由閿鄉取山路至雒南、商州，直搗賊巢，復從山陽、鎮安、洵陽馳入漢中，遏其奔軼。

translations.literal: Chengchou reasoned that with the bandits at Shang and Luo, upon hearing that government troops had arrived they would surely flee first to Hanzhong, while the main army entering by Tong Pass would end up behind them. He therefore ordered Wenzhao to take the mountain road from Wenxiang to Luonan and Shangzhou, strike straight at the bandits' lair, then gallop from Shanyang, Zhen'an, and Xunyang into Hanzhong to block their flight.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou judged that the rebels, encamped at Shang and Luo, would flee toward Hanzhong as soon as they heard government troops were coming, leaving the main army entering through Tong Pass behind them. He ordered Wenzhao to take the mountain route from Wenxiang to Luonan and Shangzhou, strike directly at the rebel stronghold, then race through Shanyang, Zhen'an, and Xunyang into Hanzhong to cut off their escape.

sentences.zh: 曰：「此行也，道路回遠，將軍甚勞苦，吾集關中兵以待將軍。

translations.literal: He said: "On this expedition the road is long and circuitous; General, you will endure great hardship. I shall assemble the Guanzhong troops to await your arrival.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "This march will take you over long and winding roads, General, and the hardship will be great. I will gather the Guanzhong troops and wait for you.

sentences.zh: 」拊其背而遣之，文詔跌馬去。

translations.literal: " He patted him on the back and sent him off. Wenzhao leapt onto his horse and departed.
translations.idiomatic: " He clapped Wenzhao on the back and sent him on his way. Wenzhao vaulted into the saddle and rode off.

sentences.zh: 五月五日抵商州。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the fifth month he reached Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the fifth month he arrived at Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊去城三十里，營火滿山。

translations.literal: The bandits were thirty li from the city; campfires filled the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were camped thirty li from the city, their fires lighting up the hills.

sentences.zh: 文詔夜半率從子參將變蛟、守備鼎蛟、都司白廣恩等敗賊深林中，追至金嶺川。

translations.literal: At midnight Wenzhao led his nephew deputy general Bianjiao, garrison commander Dingjiao, bureau commander Bai Guang'en, and others to defeat the bandits in the deep forest, pursuing them to Jinling River.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight Wenzhao led his nephew, Deputy General Cao Bianjiao, Garrison Commander Dingjiao, Bureau Commander Bai Guang'en, and others in a night attack that routed the rebels in the deep woods and chased them to Jinling River.

sentences.zh: 賊據險以千騎逆戰，變蛟大呼陷陣，諸軍並進，賊敗走。

translations.literal: The bandits held advantageous ground and met the attack with a thousand horsemen. Bianjiao shouted and charged into the enemy formation; all the armies advanced together and the bandits were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held the high ground and counterattacked with a thousand horsemen. Bianjiao shouted and plunged into their ranks; the whole force pressed forward together and drove the rebels off.

sentences.zh: 變蛟勇冠三軍，賊中聞大小曹將軍名，皆怖懾。

translations.literal: Bianjiao's courage was foremost in the three armies. Among the bandits, hearing the names of the Elder and Younger Cao Generals, all were terrified and awed.
translations.idiomatic: Bianjiao's bravery was unmatched in the army. Among the rebels, the very names of the Elder and Younger Cao Generals inspired dread.

sentences.zh: 已而闖王、八大王諸賊犯鳳翔，趨氵幵陽、隴州，文詔自漢中馳赴。

translations.literal: Before long the Chuang King, Eight Great King, and other bandits attacked Fengxiang and pressed toward Qianyang and Longzhou. Wenzhao galloped from Hanzhong to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Chuang King, Eight Great King, and other rebel leaders attacked Fengxiang and pushed toward Qianyang and Longzhou. Wenzhao raced from Hanzhong to intercept them.

sentences.zh: 賊盡向靜寧、泰安、清水、秦州間，眾且二十萬。

translations.literal: The bandits all moved toward the region between Jingning, Tai'an, Qingshui, and Qinzhou—their numbers nearing two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels converged on the country between Jingning, Tai'an, Qingshui, and Qinzhou, their numbers approaching two hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 承疇以文詔所部合張全昌、張外嘉軍止六千，眾寡不敵，告急於朝，未得命。

translations.literal: Chengchou considered that Wenzhao's force together with the armies of Zhang Quanchang and Zhang Waijia amounted to only six thousand—too few to match the enemy—and reported an emergency to the court, but received no orders.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou saw that Wenzhao's troops, combined with those of Zhang Quanchang and Zhang Waijia, numbered only six thousand—far too few to face such odds. He sent an urgent appeal to the court but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 六月，官軍遇賊亂馬川。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the government army encountered the bandits at Luanma River.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the government forces met the rebels at Luanma River.

sentences.zh: 前鋒中軍劉弘烈被執，俄副將艾萬年、柳國鎮復戰死。

translations.literal: Vanguard middle army commander Liu Honglie was captured; shortly afterward deputy generals Ai Wannian and Liu Guozhen again died fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Vanguard commander Liu Honglie was taken prisoner; soon afterward Deputy Generals Ai Wannian and Liu Guozhen were also killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 文詔聞之，瞋目大罵，亟詣承疇請行。

translations.literal: Wenzhao heard this, glared and cursed loudly, and hastened to Chengchou to request permission to go.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzhao heard the news, his eyes flashed with rage and he cursed aloud. He hurried to Chengchou and begged to be sent out.

sentences.zh: 承疇喜曰：「非將軍不能滅此賊。

translations.literal: Chengchou said joyfully: "Only the general can destroy these bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou said gladly, "Only you can destroy these rebels.

sentences.zh: 顧吾兵已分，無可策應者。

translations.literal: But my troops are already divided, and there is no one who can coordinate a response.
translations.idiomatic: But my forces are already spread thin, and I have no one left to coordinate support.

sentences.zh: 將軍行，吾將由涇陽趨淳化為後勁。

translations.literal: When the general goes, I shall hasten from Jingyang toward Chunhua as rear support.
translations.idiomatic: When you march, I will push from Jingyang toward Chunhua to cover your rear.

sentences.zh: 」文詔乃以三千人自寧州進，遇賊真寧之湫頭鎮。

translations.literal: " Wenzhao then advanced from Ningzhou with three thousand men and encountered the bandits at Qiutou Town in Zhenning.
translations.idiomatic: " Wenzhao then led three thousand men out from Ningzhou and met the rebels at Qiutou Town in Zhenning.

sentences.zh: 變蛟先登，斬首五百，追三十里，文詔率步兵繼之。

translations.literal: Bianjiao scaled the heights first, beheaded five hundred, pursued for thirty li, and Wenzhao led the infantry in follow-up.
translations.idiomatic: Bianjiao led the charge, killing five hundred rebels and pursuing them for thirty li, with Wenzhao following at the head of the infantry.

sentences.zh: 賊伏數萬騎合圍，矢猬集。

translations.literal: The bandits lay in ambush with tens of thousands of cavalry and closed in from all sides; arrows clustered thick as a hedgehog's quills.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel cavalry numbering in the tens of thousands rose from ambush and closed in from every side, arrows falling thick as a hedgehog's bristles.

sentences.zh: 賊不知為文詔也，有小卒縛急，大呼曰：「將軍救我！

translations.literal: The bandits did not know it was Wenzhao. A small soldier, bound tight, cried out loudly: "General, save me!
translations.idiomatic: The rebels did not yet know it was Wenzhao. One of his soldiers, bound fast, cried out, "General, save me!

sentences.zh: 」賊中叛卒識之，惎賊曰：「此曹總兵也。

translations.literal: " A defector among the bandits recognized him and incited the bandits: "This is Regional Commander Cao.
translations.idiomatic: " A turncoat among the rebels recognized him and shouted to the others, "This is Regional Commander Cao!

sentences.zh: 」賊喜，圍益急。

translations.literal: " The bandits rejoiced and pressed the encirclement ever tighter.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels exulted and tightened the ring around him.

sentences.zh: 文詔左右跳蕩，手擊殺數十人，轉鬥數里。

translations.literal: Wenzhao's attendants leaped and fought; with his own hands he killed several tens of men, battling for several li.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao and his men fought desperately, leaping through the press. With his own hands he killed dozens of men, battling for several li.

sentences.zh: 力不支，拔刀自刎死。

translations.literal: His strength failed; he drew his sword and cut his throat, dying.
translations.idiomatic: When his strength gave out, he drew his sword and cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 遊擊平安以下死者二十余人。

translations.literal: Roaming striker Ping'an and more than twenty others below him died.
translations.idiomatic: Roaming Striker Ping'an and more than twenty of his men also died.

sentences.zh: 承疇聞，拊膺大哭，帝亦痛悼，贈太子太保、左都督，賜祭葬，世蔭指揮僉事，有司建祠，春秋致祭。

translations.literal: When Chengchou heard, he beat his breast and wept loudly. The emperor also grieved deeply. He was posthumously awarded Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Left Chief Commander, granted sacrificial rites and burial, given hereditary enfeoffment as assistant commander, and local officials built a shrine with spring and autumn sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengchou heard the news, he beat his breast and wept. The emperor mourned deeply as well. Wenzhao was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Left Chief Commander, granted state funeral rites, and his heirs were enfeoffed as assistant commanders. Local officials built him a shrine and offered sacrifices in spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 文詔忠勇冠時，稱明季良將第一。

translations.literal: Wenzhao's loyalty and courage were foremost in his age; he was called the finest general of the late Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao's loyalty and courage were unmatched in his day, and he was hailed as the greatest general of the late Ming.

sentences.zh: 其死也，賊中為相慶。

translations.literal: At his death, the bandits celebrated one another.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the rebels celebrated among themselves.

sentences.zh: 弟文耀，從兄征討，數有功。

translations.literal: His younger brother Wenyao followed his elder brother on campaigns and repeatedly achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Wenyao accompanied him on campaign and won distinction many times.

sentences.zh: 河曲之戰，斬獲多。

translations.literal: In the battle at Hequ, many were beheaded and captured.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Hequ he took many heads and captives.

sentences.zh: 後擊賊忻州，戰死城下。

translations.literal: Later, while attacking bandits at Xinzhou, he died fighting below the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: Later, fighting rebels at Xinzhou, he was killed beneath the city walls.

sentences.zh: 詔予贈恤。

translations.literal: An edict granted posthumous honors and condolence.
translations.idiomatic: An edict awarded him posthumous honors and compensation.

sentences.zh: 從子變蛟，自有傳。

translations.literal: His nephew Bianjiao has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Bianjiao has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 周遇吉，錦州衛人。

translations.literal: Zhou Yuji was a man of Jinzhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yuji was a native of Jinzhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 少有勇力，好射生。

translations.literal: From youth he possessed courage and strength and loved hunting.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he was strong and brave and loved the hunt.

sentences.zh: 後入行伍，戰輒先登，積功至京營遊擊。

translations.literal: Later he entered the ranks; in battle he always scaled first, and through accumulated merit rose to capital-garrison roaming striker.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined the army, always first over the wall in battle, and through repeated merit rose to roaming striker in the capital garrison.

sentences.zh: 京營將多勛戚中官子弟，見遇吉質魯，意輕之。

translations.literal: The generals of the capital garrison were mostly sons of meritorious families and eunuch clients; seeing that Yuji was plain and dull, they looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the capital garrison's officers were sons of noble houses or eunuch protégés. They found Yuji coarse and unrefined and looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 遇吉曰：「公等皆紈褲子，豈足當大敵。

translations.literal: Yuji said: "You gentlemen are all silk-trousered youths—how could you be equal to a great enemy?
translations.idiomatic: Yuji said, "You are all silk-trousered dandies. How could any of you stand against a real enemy?

sentences.zh: 何不於無事時練膽勇，為異日用，而徒糜廩祿為！

translations.literal: Why not in times of peace train courage, for use on another day, rather than merely wasting grain salaries!
translations.idiomatic: Why not train your courage in peacetime, so it will serve you when the day comes, instead of wasting your rations for nothing!

sentences.zh: 」同輩鹹目笑之。

translations.literal: " His comrades all stared at him and laughed.
translations.idiomatic: " His fellow officers stared at him and laughed.

sentences.zh: 崇禎九年，都城被兵。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Chongzhen, the capital came under attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the Chongzhen reign, the capital came under attack.

sentences.zh: 從尚書張鳳翼數血戰有功，連進二秩，為前鋒營副將。

translations.literal: Following Minister Zhang Fengyi he fought bloody battles with repeated merit, was promoted two ranks in succession, and became vanguard-camp deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Minister Zhang Fengyi, he fought bloody battles again and again with notable success, was promoted two ranks in succession, and became deputy general of the vanguard camp.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，從孫應元等討賊河南，戰光山、固始，皆大捷。

translations.literal: The following winter, following Sun Yingyuan and others to suppress bandits in Henan, he fought at Guangshan and Gushi—both great victories.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter he joined Sun Yingyuan and others in suppressing rebels in Henan, winning great victories at Guangshan and Gushi.

sentences.zh: 十一年班師，進秩受賚。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the army returned to the capital; he was promoted in rank and received rewards.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the army returned to the capital, and he was promoted and rewarded.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，復出討賊，破胡可受於淅川，降其全部。

translations.literal: The following autumn he again went out to suppress bandits, defeated Hu Keshou at Xichuan, and caused his entire force to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The next autumn he marched out again against the rebels, defeated Hu Keshou at Xichuan, and accepted the surrender of his entire band.

sentences.zh: 楊嗣昌出師襄陽，遇吉從中官劉元斌往會。

translations.literal: Yang Sichang took command at Xiangyang; Yuji followed eunuch Liu Yuanbin to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Sichang took command at Xiangyang, Yuji went to join him under the eunuch Liu Yuanbin.

sentences.zh: 會張獻忠將至房縣，嗣昌策其必窺渡鄖灘，遣遇吉扼守槐樹關，張一龍屯光化，賊遂不敢犯。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhang Xianzhong was about to reach Fangxian. Sichang judged that he would surely attempt to cross at Yuntan in Yun county, and dispatched Yuji to hold Huashuguan while Zhang Yilong garrisoned Guanghua—the bandits therefore dared not attack.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xianzhong was advancing on Fangxian. Sichang predicted he would try to cross at Yuntan in Yun County and sent Yuji to hold Huashuguan while Zhang Yilong garrisoned Guanghua. The rebels did not dare approach.

sentences.zh: 十二月，獻忠敗於興安，將走竹山、竹溪，遇吉復以嗣昌令至石花街、草店扼其要害，賊自是盡入蜀。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Xianzhong was defeated at Xing'an and was about to flee toward Zhushan and Zhuxi. Yuji again, on Sichang's orders, reached Shihuajie and Caodian to block key points; the bandits thereafter all entered Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Xianzhong was defeated at Xing'an and fled toward Zhushan and Zhuxi. On Sichang's orders Yuji again took up positions at Shihuajie and Caodian to block his path, and from then on the rebels were driven entirely into Shu.

sentences.zh: 遇吉乃從元斌駐荊門，專護獻陵。

translations.literal: Yuji then followed Yuanbin to garrison Jingmen, devoted to protecting Xianling.
translations.idiomatic: Yuji then joined Yuanbin in garrisoning Jingmen, charged with guarding the Xian Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 明年與孫應元等大破羅汝才於豐邑坪。

translations.literal: The next year he joined Sun Yingyuan and others in a great defeat of Luo Rucai at Fengyiping.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he joined Sun Yingyuan and others in crushing Luo Rucai at Fengyiping.

sentences.zh: 又明年與黃得功追破賊鳳陽。

translations.literal: The year after that he joined Huang Degong in pursuing and defeating bandits at Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that he and Huang Degong pursued and routed the rebels at Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 已而旋師，敗他賊李青山於壽張，追至東平，殲滅幾盡，青山遂降。

translations.literal: Before long the army rotated back and defeated another bandit Li Qingshan at Shouzhang, pursued to Dongping, and nearly annihilated them entirely—Qingshan then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the army returned and defeated another rebel leader, Li Qingshan, at Shouzhang, pursuing him to Dongping and nearly wiping out his force. Qingshan then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 屢加太子少保、左都督。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Left Chief Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted, eventually reaching Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Left Chief Commander.

sentences.zh: 十五年冬，山西總兵官許定國有罪論死，以遇吉代之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifteenth year, Shanxi regional commander Xu Dingguo was found guilty and sentenced to death; Yuji was appointed in his place.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifteenth year Shanxi Regional Commander Xu Dingguo was found guilty and sentenced to death. Yuji was appointed to replace him.

sentences.zh: 至則汰老弱，繕甲仗，練勇敢，一軍特精。

translations.literal: Upon arrival he dismissed the old and weak, repaired armor and weapons, trained the bold, and the army became exceptionally elite.
translations.idiomatic: On taking command he weeded out the old and weak, repaired arms and armor, drilled the brave, and turned the army into an exceptionally sharp force.

sentences.zh: 明年十二月，李自成陷全陜，將犯山西。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the following year, Li Zicheng captured all of Shaanxi and was about to invade Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the following year Li Zicheng conquered all of Shaanxi and prepared to invade Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 遇吉以沿河千餘里，賊處處可渡，分兵扼其上流，以下流蒲阪屬之巡撫蔡懋德，而請濟師於朝。

translations.literal: Yuji considered that along the river for more than a thousand li the bandits could cross anywhere; he divided his troops to hold the upper reaches, entrusted the lower reaches at Puban to Grand Coordinator Cai Maode, and requested reinforcements from the court.
translations.idiomatic: Yuji saw that along more than a thousand li of river the rebels could cross almost anywhere. He split his forces to hold the upper reaches, left the lower crossing at Puban to Grand Coordinator Cai Maode, and asked the court for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣副將熊通以二千人來赴。

translations.literal: The court dispatched Deputy General Xiong Tong with two thousand men to come to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Deputy General Xiong Tong with two thousand men to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 十七年正月，遇吉令通防河。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventeenth year, Yuji ordered Tong to defend the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventeenth year Yuji ordered Xiong Tong to defend the river.

sentences.zh: 會平陽守將陳尚智已遣使迎賊，諷通還鎮說降。

translations.literal: It happened that Pingyang garrison commander Chen Shangzhi had already sent envoys to welcome the bandits and subtly urged Tong to return to his post to urge surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyang's garrison commander Chen Shangzhi had already sent envoys to welcome the rebels and quietly urged Xiong Tong to return to his post and negotiate surrender.

sentences.zh: 遇吉叱之曰：「吾受國厚恩，寧從爾叛逆！

translations.literal: Yuji berated him: "I have received great grace from the state—would I follow you in rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: Yuji rebuked him sharply: "I owe the state a great debt of gratitude. Would I join you in rebellion!

sentences.zh: 且爾統兵二千，不能殺賊，反作說客邪！

translations.literal: And you command two thousand troops yet cannot kill bandits, but instead act as envoys of persuasion!
translations.idiomatic: And you command two thousand troops, yet instead of killing rebels you come as a negotiator!

sentences.zh: 」立斬之，傳首京師。

translations.literal: " He immediately beheaded him and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: " He had him beheaded on the spot and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 至二月七日，太原陷，懋德死之。

translations.literal: By the seventh day of the second month, Taiyuan fell and Maode died there.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the second month Taiyuan fell, and Maode died defending it.

sentences.zh: 賊遂陷忻州，圍代州。

translations.literal: The bandits then captured Xinzhou and besieged Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then took Xinzhou and laid siege to Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 遇吉先在代遏其北犯，乃憑城固守，而潛出兵奮擊。

translations.literal: Yuji had previously blocked their northern advance at Dai; now he relied on the city for stout defense while secretly sending troops out in fierce strikes.
translations.idiomatic: Yuji had already blocked their northward advance at Daizhou. He held the city in a stubborn defense while secretly sending troops out in fierce counterattacks.

sentences.zh: 連數日，殺賊無算。

translations.literal: For several days in succession, they killed bandits beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: For days on end they killed rebels beyond count.

sentences.zh: 會食盡援絕，退保寧武。

translations.literal: When provisions were exhausted and reinforcements cut off, they withdrew to defend Ningwu.
translations.idiomatic: When food ran out and relief failed to come, they fell back to hold Ningwu.

sentences.zh: 賊亦踵至，大呼五日不降者屠其城。

translations.literal: The bandits also followed close behind, shouting that if there was no surrender within five days they would massacre the city.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels followed close behind, shouting that if the city did not surrender within five days they would slaughter every soul in it.

sentences.zh: 遇吉四面發大炮，殺賊萬人，火藥且盡，外圍轉急。

translations.literal: Yuji fired great cannon on all four sides, killing ten thousand bandits. Gunpowder was nearly spent and the outer encirclement grew ever tighter.
translations.idiomatic: Yuji answered with heavy cannon on every side, killing ten thousand rebels. But gunpowder ran low and the siege tightened.

sentences.zh: 或請甘言紿之，遇吉怒曰：「若輩何怯邪！

translations.literal: Some suggested coaxing them with fair words. Yuji said angrily: "You people—why so timid!
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to stall the rebels with smooth words. Yuji snapped, "Why are you all so cowardly!

sentences.zh: 今能勝，一軍皆忠義。

translations.literal: If we can win now, the whole army will be loyal and righteous.
translations.idiomatic: If we win now, every man in this army will have proved his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 即不支，縛我予賊。

translations.literal: If we cannot hold, bind me and hand me to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: If we cannot hold, bind me and hand me over to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 」於是設伏城內，出弱卒誘賊入城，亟下閘殺數千人。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he set an ambush inside the city, sent out weak troops to lure the bandits into the city, quickly lowered the gate, and killed several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: " He then laid an ambush inside the city, sent out a few weak troops to lure the rebels in, and when they entered slammed the gates shut and killed several thousand.

sentences.zh: 賊用炮攻城，圮復完者再，傷其四驍將。

translations.literal: The bandits used cannon to attack the city; twice the walls were breached and twice repaired; four of their fiercest generals were wounded.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels bombarded the walls with cannon. Twice the walls were breached and twice repaired, and four of their best generals were wounded.

sentences.zh: 自成懼，欲退。

translations.literal: Zicheng grew afraid and wished to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng grew alarmed and wanted to pull back.

sentences.zh: 其將曰：「我眾百倍於彼，但用十攻一，番進，蔑不勝矣。

translations.literal: His generals said: "Our numbers are a hundred times theirs. We need only use ten to attack one, advancing in rotation—we cannot fail to win.
translations.idiomatic: His commanders said, "We outnumber them a hundred to one. Send ten men against each defender, wave after wave, and we cannot fail.

sentences.zh: 」自成從之。

translations.literal: " Zicheng followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Zicheng agreed.

sentences.zh: 前隊死，後復繼。

translations.literal: The front ranks died; those behind continued to advance.
translations.idiomatic: The front ranks fell, and those behind pressed forward to take their place.

sentences.zh: 官軍力盡，城遂陷。

translations.literal: The government army's strength was spent and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders exhausted their strength, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 遇吉巷戰，馬蹶，徒步跳蕩，手格殺數十人。

translations.literal: Yuji fought in the alleys; his horse stumbled and he fought on foot, leaping and striking, with his hands killing several tens of men.
translations.idiomatic: Yuji fought street by street. His horse went down, but he fought on foot, leaping through the alleys and killing dozens of men with his bare hands.

sentences.zh: 身被矢如猬，竟為賊執，大罵不屈。

translations.literal: His body was pierced by arrows like a hedgehog; ultimately he was captured by the bandits and cursed them loudly without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Arrows studded his body like a hedgehog's quills. At last the rebels seized him, but he cursed them without bending.

sentences.zh: 賊懸之高竿，叢射殺之，復臠其肉。

translations.literal: The bandits hung him on a tall pole, rained arrows on him and killed him, then cut his flesh into pieces.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels hung him from a tall pole, riddled him with arrows, and then cut his flesh to pieces.

sentences.zh: 城中士民感遇吉忠義，巷戰殺賊，不可勝計。

translations.literal: The gentry and people of the city, moved by Yuji's loyalty and righteousness, fought in the alleys and killed bandits beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Inspired by Yuji's loyalty, the city's soldiers and civilians fought in the streets and killed rebels beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 其舍中兒，先從遇吉出鬥，死亡略盡。

translations.literal: The boys in his household, who had first followed Yuji out to fight, were nearly all dead.
translations.idiomatic: The young retainers in his household who had marched out with him were nearly all killed.

sentences.zh: 夫人劉氏素勇健，率婦女數十人據山巔公廨，登屋而射，每一矢斃一賊，賊不敢逼。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Liu was by nature brave and strong; she led several tens of women to hold the public yamen on the mountaintop, climbed onto roofs and shot—each arrow felled one bandit, and the bandits did not dare approach.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Liu, was herself bold and strong. She led several dozen women to hold the public office on the hilltop, climbed onto the rooftops, and shot down a rebel with every arrow. None dared come near.

sentences.zh: 縱火焚之，闔家盡死。

translations.literal: They set fire and burned them; the entire family perished.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels set fire to the building and burned them all. The whole household perished.

sentences.zh: 自成集眾計曰：「寧武雖破，吾將士死傷多。

translations.literal: Zicheng gathered the multitude and deliberated: "Although Ningwu is broken, my officers and soldiers have suffered many dead and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng assembled his commanders and said, "We have taken Ningwu, but my officers and men have suffered heavy losses.

sentences.zh: 自此達京師，歷大同、陽和、宣府、居庸，皆有重兵。

translations.literal: From here to the capital, passing Datong, Yanghe, Xuanfu, and Juyong, there are heavy garrisons everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: From here to the capital we must pass Datong, Yanghe, Xuanfu, and Juyong—every one of them heavily garrisoned.

sentences.zh: 倘盡如寧武，吾部下寧有孑遺哉！

translations.literal: If they are all like Ningwu, will any of my followers survive!
translations.idiomatic: If every city fights like Ningwu, will any of my men be left alive!

sentences.zh: 不如還秦休息，圖後舉。

translations.literal: Better to return to Qin to rest and plan a later effort.
translations.idiomatic: Better to withdraw to Qin, recover our strength, and plan the next move.

sentences.zh: 」刻期將遁，而大同總兵姜襄降表至，自成大喜。

translations.literal: " He fixed a date to withdraw, but the submission memorial from Datong regional commander Jiang Xiang arrived, and Zicheng was greatly delighted.
translations.idiomatic: " He had fixed a date for withdrawal, but then the surrender petition from Jiang Xiang, regional commander at Datong, arrived—and Zicheng was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 方宴其使者，宣府總兵王承蔭表亦至，自成益喜。

translations.literal: Just as he was feasting the envoy, the submission memorial from Xuanfu regional commander Wang Chengyin also arrived, and Zicheng was even more pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He was still feasting the envoy when Wang Chengyin's surrender petition arrived from Xuanfu as well, and Zicheng's delight only grew.

sentences.zh: 遂決策長驅，歷大同、宣府抵居庸。

translations.literal: He then decided on a long drive, passing through Datong and Xuanfu to reach Juyong.
translations.idiomatic: He then resolved to drive straight through, passing Datong and Xuanfu until he reached Juyong.

sentences.zh: 太監杜之秩、總兵唐通復開門延之，京師遂不守矣。

translations.literal: Eunuch Du Zhiji and regional commander Tang Tong again opened the gates to welcome them, and the capital could no longer be held.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Du Zhiji and regional commander Tang Tong opened the gates to them once more, and the capital was lost.

sentences.zh: 賊每語人曰：「他鎮復有一周總兵，吾安得至此。

translations.literal: The bandits often said to people: "If every garrison had another Regional Commander Zhou, how could I have reached here?
translations.idiomatic: The rebels would often say to people, "If every garrison had another Regional Commander Zhou, how could I ever have reached here?

sentences.zh: 」福王時，贈太保，謚忠武，列祀旌忠祠。

translations.literal: " In the time of the Prince of Fu, [Yuji] was posthumously granted Grand Guardian, given the posthumous title Zhongwu, and entered for sacrifice at the Jingzhong Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: " Under the Prince of Fu, Yuji was posthumously made Grand Guardian, given the posthumous title Zhongwu, and enshrined for sacrifice at the Jingzhong Shrine.

sentences.zh: 黃得功，號虎山，開原衛人，其先自合肥徙。

translations.literal: Huang Degong, styled Hushan, was a native of Kaiyuan Guard; his forebears had moved from Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Degong, styled Hushan, came from Kaiyuan Guard. His family had originally moved there from Hefei.

sentences.zh: 早孤，與母徐居。

translations.literal: He lost his father early and lived with his mother, née Xu.
translations.idiomatic: His father died while he was young, and he lived with his mother, Lady Xu.

sentences.zh: 少負奇氣，膽略過人。

translations.literal: As a youth he possessed an unusual spirit; his courage and strategy surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he had an uncommon spirit, and his courage and daring outstripped those around him.

sentences.zh: 年十二，母釀酒熟，竊飲至盡。

translations.literal: At age twelve, when his mother's wine had finished fermenting, he secretly drank it all.
translations.idiomatic: When he was twelve, his mother finished brewing a batch of wine, and he secretly drank every drop.

sentences.zh: 母責之，笑曰：「償易耳。

translations.literal: His mother scolded him; he laughed and said: "Paying it back will be easy.
translations.idiomatic: His mother scolded him. He only laughed and said, "Paying it back will be easy.

sentences.zh: 」時遼事急，得功持刀雜行伍中，出斬首二級，中賞率得白金五十兩，歸奉母，曰：「兒以償酒也。

translations.literal: " At that time the Liaodong situation was urgent. Degong took up a blade and mingled among the ranks; on an expedition he beheaded two enemies and received the standard reward of fifty taels of white silver. He returned and presented it to his mother, saying: "Your son has paid for the wine.
translations.idiomatic: " The Liaodong frontier was then in crisis. Degong took up a sword, mixed in among the ranks, and on campaign cut off two enemy heads. By the usual reward scale he received fifty taels of silver. He brought it home to his mother and said, "Your son has paid for the wine.

sentences.zh: 」由是隸經略為親軍，累功至遊擊。

translations.literal: " From this he entered the frontier commissioner's personal guard and, accumulating merit, rose to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: " From then on he served in the frontier commissioner's personal guard, and by accumulated merit rose to the rank of colonel.

sentences.zh: 崇禎九年，遷副總兵，分管京衛管。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Chongzhen, he was transferred to vice regional commander, assigned to manage the capital guard sector.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 9 he was promoted to vice regional commander and put in charge of a sector of the capital guard.

sentences.zh: 十一年以禁軍從總督熊文燦擊賊於舞陽，鏖光、固間，最。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, leading imperial guards he followed Grand Coordinator Xiong Wencan to strike bandits at Wuyang; in the fierce fighting around Guang and Gu, he was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he led imperial guards under Grand Coordinator Xiong Wencan against rebels at Wuyang, and in the bitter fighting around Guang and Gu he distinguished himself above all.

sentences.zh: 八月又從擊賊馬光玉於淅川之吳村、王家寨，大破之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he again followed to strike the bandit Ma Guangyu at Wucun and Wangjiazhai in Xichuan, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he again joined the campaign and routed the rebel Ma Guangyu at Wucun and Wangjiazhai in Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 詔加太子太師，署總兵銜。

translations.literal: An edict added him as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and gave him acting regional commander rank.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made him Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and gave him acting regional commander rank.

sentences.zh: 十三年從太監盧九德破賊於板石畈，賊革裹眼等五營降。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he followed eunuch Lu Jiude to defeat bandits at Banshi Fan; five camps including Ge Guayan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he followed the eunuch Lu Jiude to defeat rebels at Banshi Fan, after which five rebel camps, including Ge Guayan's, surrendered.

sentences.zh: 十四年以總兵與王憲分護鳳陽、泗州陵，得功駐定遠。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, as regional commander, he and Wang Xian jointly protected the tombs at Fengyang and Sizhou; Degong was stationed at Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, as regional commander, he and Wang Xian were assigned jointly to guard the imperial tombs at Fengyang and Sizhou, with Degong stationed at Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 張獻忠攻桐城，挾營將廖應登至城下誘降。

translations.literal: Zhang Xianzhong attacked Tongcheng, bringing camp officer Liao Yingdeng to the foot of the wall to induce surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xianzhong besieged Tongcheng and brought the camp officer Liao Yingdeng to the foot of the wall to coax the city into surrender.

sentences.zh: 得功與劉良佐合兵擊之於鮑家嶺，賊敗遁，追至潛山，擒斬賊將闖世王馬武、三鷂子王興國。

translations.literal: Degong and Liu Liangzuo combined forces and struck them at Baojia Ridge; the bandits were defeated and fled. Pursuing to Qianshan, they captured and executed the bandit generals Chuangshi Wang Ma Wu and Third Sparrow Hawk Wang Xingguo.
translations.idiomatic: Degong and Liu Liangzuo joined forces and struck them at Baojia Ridge. The rebels broke and fled. The pursuit reached Qianshan, where they captured and executed the rebel generals Chuangshi Wang Ma Wu and Third Sparrow Hawk Wang Xingguo.

sentences.zh: 三鷂子，獻忠養子，最號驍勇者也。

translations.literal: Third Sparrow Hawk was Xianzhong's adopted son and was said to be the fiercest and bravest.
translations.idiomatic: Third Sparrow Hawk was Xianzhong's adopted son and was regarded as the fiercest fighter in his ranks.

sentences.zh: 得功箭傷面，愈自奮，與賊轉戰十余日，所殺傷獨多。

translations.literal: Degong was wounded in the face by an arrow but fought all the harder; he battled the bandits back and forth for more than ten days, killing and wounding more than any other.
translations.idiomatic: An arrow struck Degong in the face, but he fought all the harder. For more than ten days he battled the rebels back and forth, and none killed or wounded more than he.

sentences.zh: 明年移鎮廬州。

translations.literal: The following year he was transferred to garrison Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was transferred to garrison Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 十七年封靖南伯。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was enfeoffed as Baron of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was enfeoffed as Baron of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 福王立江南，進封侯。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu established himself in Jiangnan, [Degong] was promoted to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu established his court in Jiangnan, Degong was promoted to marquis.

sentences.zh: 旋命與劉良佐、劉澤清、高傑為四鎮。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was ordered, together with Liu Liangzuo, Liu Zeqing, and Gao Jie, to form the Four Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered, together with Liu Liangzuo, Liu Zeqing, and Gao Jie, to serve as one of the Four Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 初，督輔史可法慮傑跋扈難制，故置得功儀真，陰相牽制。

translations.literal: At first, supervising secretary Shi Kefa feared that Jie was overbearing and hard to control, so he posted Degong at Yizhen to restrain him in secret.
translations.idiomatic: At first Supervising Secretary Shi Kefa feared that Gao Jie was too overbearing to control, so he posted Degong at Yizhen to keep him in check.

sentences.zh: 適登萊總兵黃蜚將之任，蜚與得功同姓，稱兄弟，移書請兵備非常。

translations.literal: Just then, Deng-Lai regional commander Huang Fei was about to take up his post. Fei shared the Huang surname with Degong and called themselves brothers; he sent a letter asking for extraordinary military preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Huang Fei, the new regional commander of Deng-Lai, was on his way to take up his post. He shared the Huang surname with Degong and treated him as a sworn brother, and wrote asking for extraordinary military support.

sentences.zh: 得功率騎三百由揚州往高郵迎之，傑副將胡茂楨馳報傑。

translations.literal: Degong led three hundred cavalry from Yangzhou toward Gaoyou to welcome him; Jie's deputy Hu Maozhen galloped to report to Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Degong led three hundred cavalry from Yangzhou toward Gaoyou to welcome him. Gao Jie's deputy Hu Maozhen galloped ahead to warn Jie.

sentences.zh: 傑素忌得功，又疑圖己，乃伏精卒道中，邀擊之。

translations.literal: Jie had long envied Degong and now suspected a plot against himself; he therefore hid elite troops along the road and ambushed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jie had long resented Degong and now suspected a plot against himself, so he hid picked troops along the road and ambushed him.

sentences.zh: 得功行至土橋，方作食，伏起，出不意，上馬舉鐵鞭，飛矢雨集，馬踣，騰他騎馳。

translations.literal: Degong reached Tugiao Bridge and was eating when the ambush rose. Taken by surprise, he mounted, raised his iron whip, and arrows fell like rain. His horse collapsed; he leaped onto another mount and galloped away.
translations.idiomatic: Degong reached Tugiao Bridge and was taking a meal when the ambush sprang up. Caught off guard, he mounted, raised his iron whip, and arrows fell like rain. His horse went down, but he vaulted onto another and galloped away.

sentences.zh: 有驍騎舞槊直前，得功大呼，反鬥，挾其槊而抶之，人馬皆糜。

translations.literal: A fierce cavalryman twirling a lance charged straight at him. Degong shouted, turned to fight, seized his lance and struck him with it—man and horse alike were crushed to pulp.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce rider came at him twirling a lance. Degong roared, wheeled to meet him, seized the lance, and struck him down with it until man and horse alike were crushed to pulp.

sentences.zh: 復殺數十人，跳入頹垣中，哮聲如雷，追者不敢進，遂疾馳至大軍，得免。

translations.literal: He killed several tens more, leaped into a crumbling wall, and roared like thunder. The pursuers did not dare advance; he then galloped at speed to the main force and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He killed several dozen more, then leaped into a ruined wall and roared like thunder. The pursuers dared not come closer. He raced back to the main body of his army and escaped.

sentences.zh: 方鬥時，傑潛師搗儀真，得功兵頗傷，而所俱行三百騎皆歿。

translations.literal: While he was fighting, Jie secretly sent troops to strike Yizhen. Degong's army suffered considerable casualties, and all three hundred cavalry who had accompanied him perished.
translations.idiomatic: While he was fighting, Jie secretly sent troops to strike Yizhen. Degong's army took heavy losses, and all three hundred cavalry who had ridden out with him were killed.

sentences.zh: 遂訴於朝，願與傑決一死戰。

translations.literal: He then appealed to the court, declaring his wish to settle the matter with Jie in a fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: He appealed to the court and asked to settle the matter with Jie in a fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 可法命監軍萬元吉和解之，不可。

translations.literal: Kefa ordered military inspector Wan Yuanji to mediate, but [Degong] would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa ordered the military inspector Wan Yuanji to mediate, but Degong would not accept it.

sentences.zh: 會得功有母喪，可法來吊，語之曰：「土橋之役，無智愚皆知傑不義。

translations.literal: Just then Degong was mourning his mother. Kefa came to offer condolences and said to him: "At the battle of Tugiao Bridge, wise and foolish alike know that Jie acted unjustly.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Degong was in mourning for his mother. Kefa came to offer condolences and said to him, "At Tugiao Bridge, everyone from the wise to the simple knows that Gao Jie acted unjustly.

sentences.zh: 今將軍以國故捐盛怒，而歸曲於高，是將軍收大名於天下也。

translations.literal: Now, General, if for the sake of the state you set aside your great anger and yield the grievance to Gao, you will win great renown throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: If now, for the sake of the state, you set aside your great anger and yield the grievance to Gao, you will win great renown throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 」得功色稍和，終以所殺亡多為恨。

translations.literal: " Degong's expression softened somewhat, but in the end he still grieved the many who had been killed.
translations.idiomatic: " Degong's face softened a little, but in the end he still brooded over the many men who had been killed.

sentences.zh: 可法令傑償其馬，復出千金為母赗。

translations.literal: Kefa ordered Jie to compensate him for his horses and also gave a thousand taels of gold as funeral offerings for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa ordered Jie to replace his horses and also gave a thousand taels of gold as funeral offerings for his mother.

sentences.zh: 得功不得已，聽之。

translations.literal: Degong, with no alternative, accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Degong, having no choice, accepted.

sentences.zh: 明年，傑欲趨河南，規取中原。

translations.literal: The following year Jie wished to advance toward Henan and plan the recovery of the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Gao Jie wanted to push into Henan and plan the recovery of the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 詔得功與劉良佐守邳、徐。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Degong and Liu Liangzuo to guard Pi and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Degong and Liu Liangzuo to hold Pi and Xu.

sentences.zh: 傑死，得功還儀真。

translations.literal: When Jie died, Degong returned to Yizhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Jie died, Degong returned to Yizhen.

sentences.zh: 傑家並將士妻子尚留揚州，得功謀襲之。

translations.literal: Jie's family and the wives and children of his officers and soldiers still remained in Yangzhou; Degong plotted to raid them.
translations.idiomatic: Jie's family and the wives and children of his officers and soldiers were still in Yangzhou, and Degong plotted to raid them.

sentences.zh: 朝廷急遣盧九德諭止，得功遂移鎮廬州。

translations.literal: The court urgently dispatched Lu Jiude to persuade him to stop, and Degong then transferred his garrison to Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court urgently sent Lu Jiude to stop him, and Degong then moved his garrison to Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 四月，左良玉東下，以請君側為名，至九江，病死，軍中立其子夢庚。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Zuo Liangyu marched eastward under the pretext of removing evil ministers at the emperor's side. Reaching Jiujiang, he died of illness, and the army installed his son Menggeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Zuo Liangyu marched east under the pretext of clearing evil from the emperor's side. He reached Jiujiang, died of illness, and the army installed his son Menggeng in his place.

sentences.zh: 命得功趨上江禦之，駐師荻港。
