translations.literal: Degong was ordered to hurry upriver to resist him and encamped at Digang.
translations.idiomatic: Degong was ordered to hurry upriver to oppose him and encamped at Digang.

sentences.zh: 得功破夢庚於銅陵，解其圍。

translations.literal: Degong defeated Menggeng at Tongling and lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Degong defeated Menggeng at Tongling and broke the siege.

sentences.zh: 命移家鎮太平，一意辦賊，論功加左柱國。

translations.literal: He was ordered to move his household and garrison Taiping, devoting himself entirely to dealing with the enemy; for his merit he was given the rank of Left Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to move his household and garrison Taiping, devoting himself entirely to fighting the enemy, and for his merit was made Left Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 時大清兵已渡江，知福王奔，分兵襲太平。

translations.literal: By then Qing troops had already crossed the Yangtze. Learning that the Prince of Fu had fled, they divided their forces to assault Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: By then Qing troops had already crossed the Yangtze. Learning that the Prince of Fu had fled, they split their forces and struck at Taiping.

sentences.zh: 得功方收兵屯蕪湖，福王潛入其營。

translations.literal: Degong was just gathering his troops and encamping at Wuhu when the Prince of Fu slipped secretly into his camp.
translations.idiomatic: Degong was just gathering his troops at Wuhu when the Prince of Fu slipped secretly into his camp.

sentences.zh: 得功驚泣曰：「陛下死守京城，臣等猶可盡力，奈何聽奸人言，倉卒到此！

translations.literal: Degong cried out in shock: "Your Majesty, if you had held the capital to the death, we could still have done our utmost—why heed the words of villainous men and come here in such haste!
translations.idiomatic: Degong cried out in shock and grief, "Your Majesty, if you had held the capital to the death, we could still have done our utmost. Why listen to villainous counsel and come here in such haste!

sentences.zh: 且臣方對敵，安能扈駕？

translations.literal: Moreover, I am facing the enemy—how can I escort Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: And I am facing the enemy now—how can I escort Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「非卿無可仗者。

translations.literal: " The Prince said: "There is no one else I can rely on but you.
translations.idiomatic: " The Prince said, "There is no one else I can rely on but you.

sentences.zh: 」得功泣曰：「願效死。

translations.literal: " Degong wept and said: "I am willing to give my life.
translations.idiomatic: " Degong wept and said, "Then I am willing to die in your service.

sentences.zh: 」得功戰荻港時，傷臂幾墮。

translations.literal: " When Degong had fought at Digang, his arm had been wounded so badly it nearly fell off.
translations.idiomatic: " He had already fought at Digang with an arm so badly wounded it nearly came off.

sentences.zh: 衣葛衣，以帛絡臂，佩刀坐小舟，督麾下八總兵結束前迎敵。

translations.literal: Clad in hempen garments, with silk binding his arm, sword at his belt, he sat in a small boat and directed his eight regional commanders to arm themselves and advance to meet the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Clad in plain hemp, his arm bound with silk, sword at his belt, he sat in a small boat and ordered his eight regional commanders to arm themselves and advance to meet the enemy.

sentences.zh: 而劉良佐已先歸命，大呼岸上招降。

translations.literal: But Liu Liangzuo had already surrendered first and shouted from the shore, urging them to submit.
translations.idiomatic: But Liu Liangzuo had already surrendered and was shouting from the shore, urging them to submit.

sentences.zh: 得功怒叱曰：「汝乃降乎！

translations.literal: Degong roared in rebuke: "You would surrender!
translations.idiomatic: Degong roared in rebuke, "You would surrender!

sentences.zh: 」忽飛矢至，中其喉偏左。

translations.literal: " Suddenly a flying arrow came and struck him slightly left of the throat.
translations.idiomatic: " Suddenly a flying arrow struck him just to the left of the throat.

sentences.zh: 得功知不可為，擲刀拾所拔箭刺吭死。

translations.literal: Degong knew all was lost. He cast aside his sword, picked up the arrow he had drawn out, and stabbed himself in the throat to die.
translations.idiomatic: Degong knew all was lost. He cast aside his sword, took the arrow he had pulled out, and drove it into his throat.

sentences.zh: 其妻聞之，亦自經。

translations.literal: When his wife heard of it, she hanged herself as well.
translations.idiomatic: When his wife heard of it, she hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 總兵翁之琪投江死，中軍田雄遂挾福王降。

translations.literal: Regional commander Weng Zhiqi threw himself into the river and died; staff officer Tian Xiong then seized the Prince of Fu and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Weng Zhiqi threw himself into the river and died. Staff officer Tian Xiong then seized the Prince of Fu and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 得功粗猛不識文義。

translations.literal: Degong was rough and fierce and did not understand literary meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Degong was rough and fierce and had little understanding of written language.

sentences.zh: 江南初立，王詔書指揮，多出群小。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was first established, the Prince's edicts and commands were mostly issued by petty men.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiangnan court was first established, the Prince's edicts and orders mostly came from petty men at court.

sentences.zh: 得功得詔紙或對使罵裂之。

translations.literal: When Degong received an edict, he would sometimes curse the envoy and tear it to pieces.
translations.idiomatic: When Degong received an edict, he would sometimes curse the messenger and tear the paper to shreds.

sentences.zh: 然忠義出天性，聞以國事相規誡者，輒屈己改不旋踵。

translations.literal: Yet loyalty and righteousness came from his inborn nature. When he heard someone admonish him on state affairs, he would humble himself and reform without delay.
translations.idiomatic: Yet loyalty and righteousness were in his nature. When anyone admonished him on matters of state, he would humble himself and change at once.

sentences.zh: 北來太子之獄，得功抗疏爭曰：「東宮未必假冒，先帝子即上子，未有了無證明，混然雷同者。

translations.literal: In the case of the crown prince who had come from the north, Degong submitted a remonstrance saying: "The Eastern Palace may not necessarily be an impostor. A son of the late emperor is a son of the present sovereign; it is not that there is no proof at all, yet all alike echo the same line.
translations.idiomatic: In the case of the crown prince who had arrived from the north, Degong submitted a remonstrance saying, "The Eastern Palace may not necessarily be an impostor. A son of the late emperor is a son of the present sovereign. It is not that there is no evidence at all, yet everyone echoes the same line.

sentences.zh: 臣恐在廷諸臣，諂徇者多，抗顏者少，即明白識認，亦不敢抗詞取禍矣。

translations.literal: I fear that among the officials at court, those who flatter and yield are many while those who confront authority are few—even if they clearly recognize the truth, they dare not speak against it and invite disaster.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that at court those who flatter and yield are many and those who speak plainly are few. Even if they clearly recognize the truth, they dare not argue against it and invite disaster.

sentences.zh: 」時太子真偽莫敢決，而得功忠憤不阿如此。

translations.literal: " At that time none dared decide whether the crown prince was genuine or false, yet Degong's loyal indignation and refusal to bow were such as this.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time none dared settle whether the crown prince was genuine or false, yet Degong's loyal indignation and refusal to bow were such as this.

sentences.zh: 得功每戰，飲酒數鬥，酒酣氣益厲。

translations.literal: Before every battle Degong drank several pecks of wine; when the wine had taken hold, his spirit grew fiercer still.
translations.idiomatic: Before every battle Degong drank several pecks of wine, and once the wine had taken hold his fighting spirit grew fiercer still.

sentences.zh: 喜持鐵鞭戰，鞭漬血沾手腕，以水濡之，久乃得脫，軍中呼為黃闖子。

translations.literal: He liked to fight wielding an iron whip. When blood soaked the whip and clung to his wrist, he would wet it with water and only after a long while could it be pulled free. The army called him Yellow Crasher.
translations.idiomatic: He liked to fight with an iron whip. When blood soaked the whip and clung to his wrist, he had to wet it with water before it could finally be pulled free. The army called him Yellow Crasher.

sentences.zh: 始為偏裨，隨大帥立功名，未嘗一當大敵。

translations.literal: At first, as a junior officer, he followed great commanders to build merit and had never once faced a major enemy alone.
translations.idiomatic: At first, as a junior officer, he followed great commanders to win distinction and had never once borne the brunt of a major enemy alone.

sentences.zh: 及專鎮封侯，不及一年余而南北轉徙，主逃將潰，無所一用其力，束手就殪，與國俱亡而已。

translations.literal: But once he held independent command and was enfeoffed as a marquis, in little more than a year he was driven north and south in constant movement—the ruler fled, the troops collapsed, and he had nowhere to bring his strength fully to bear. He was slaughtered with folded hands, perishing together with the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: But once he held independent command and was enfeoffed as a marquis, in little more than a year he was driven back and forth across north and south—the ruler fled, the armies collapsed, and he had nowhere to bring his full strength to bear. He was cut down with his hands tied, and perished together with the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 其軍行紀律嚴，下無敢犯，所至人感其德。

translations.literal: His army marched under strict discipline; none below dared violate it, and wherever he went the people were moved by his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: His army marched under strict discipline, none below dared violate it, and wherever he went the people were moved by his virtue.

sentences.zh: 廬州、桐城、定遠皆為立生祠。

translations.literal: Living shrines were erected to him in Luzhou, Tongcheng, and Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Living shrines were erected to him in Luzhou, Tongcheng, and Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 葬儀真方山母墓側。

translations.literal: He was buried on Mount Fang in Yizhen, beside his mother's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried on Mount Fang in Yizhen, beside his mother's tomb.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：曹文詔等秉驍猛之資，所向摧敗，皆所稱萬人敵也。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Cao Wenzhao and the others possessed fierce and valiant gifts; wherever they turned they shattered the foe—they were all men called a match for ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Cao Wenzhao and the others possessed fierce and valiant gifts. Wherever they turned they shattered the foe—they were all men reckoned a match for ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 大命既傾，良將顛蹶。

translations.literal: When the great mandate had already toppled, good generals stumbled and fell.
translations.idiomatic: When the great mandate had already toppled, good generals stumbled and fell.

sentences.zh: 三人者忠勇最著，死事亦最烈，故別著於篇。

translations.literal: Of the three, their loyalty and courage were most outstanding and their deaths in service most fierce; therefore they are set apart in a separate account within this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Of the three, their loyalty and courage stood out most, and their deaths in service were the fiercest; therefore they are given a separate account in this chapter.
